# S3 Bucket Events

The `s3` event invokes a Lambda function when objects change in an Amazon S3 bucket, through the bucket's event notifications. By default, the Framework creates the bucket with the notification configuration. With `existing: true`, it adds the notifications to a bucket that already exists.

This `serverless.yml` creates a bucket and invokes `resize` for every object created in it:

```yaml
# serverless.yml
service: my-service

provider:
  name: aws
  runtime: nodejs24.x

functions:
  resize:
    handler: handler.resize
    events:
      - s3: my-service-${sls:stage}-photos
```

S3 invokes the function asynchronously. Each record names the bucket and the object key; the key is URL-encoded, so a space arrives as `+`:

```javascript
// handler.mjs
export const resize = async (event) => {
  for (const record of event.Records) {
    const bucket = record.s3.bucket.name
    const key = decodeURIComponent(record.s3.object.key.replace(/\+/g, ' '))
    console.log(record.eventName, bucket, key)
  }
}
```

Bucket names are unique across all AWS accounts, so include the service and stage in the name, as in the example. A name must follow the [S3 bucket naming rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucketnamingrules.html); the Framework stops packaging on a name that doesn't. A function that writes to the bucket that triggers it can invoke itself in a loop; write to another bucket, or limit the trigger with a [prefix rule](#setting-filter-rules).

## Setting the specific trigger event

The `s3` event's `event` sets the S3 event type that invokes the function. Without it, the Framework uses `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, which covers every way an object is created, including overwriting an existing object. This function runs whenever an object is deleted:

```yaml
functions:
  users:
    handler: handler.users
    events:
      - s3:
          bucket: my-service-${sls:stage}-photos
          event: s3:ObjectRemoved:*
```

`event` takes one S3 event type, starting with `s3:`, such as `s3:ObjectCreated:Put`, `s3:ObjectRemoved:Delete`, `s3:ObjectRestore:Completed` or `s3:ObjectTagging:*`. For the full list, see [Supported event types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html#supported-notification-event-types). To react to several event types, add one `s3` event for each.

## Setting filter rules

The `s3` event's `rules` limits the notification to object keys with a given prefix, suffix, or both. This function runs for `.jpg` objects created under `uploads/`:

```yaml
functions:
  users:
    handler: handler.users
    events:
      - s3:
          bucket: my-service-${sls:stage}-photos
          event: s3:ObjectCreated:*
          rules:
            - prefix: uploads/
            - suffix: .jpg
```

Each item in `rules` has exactly one key, `prefix` or `suffix`, with a string or a CloudFormation intrinsic function as its value. S3 doesn't accept a `*` wildcard in a prefix or suffix, and other special characters must be URL-encoded. See [Configuring event notifications using object key name filtering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-filtering.html).

## Several functions or events on one bucket

A bucket can invoke several functions, and one function can have several `s3` events on the same bucket. The Framework combines them into the bucket's notification configuration:

```yaml
functions:
  users:
    handler: handler.users
    events:
      - s3:
          bucket: my-service-${sls:stage}-photos
          event: s3:ObjectCreated:*
          rules:
            - prefix: uploads/
      - s3:
          bucket: my-service-${sls:stage}-photos
          event: s3:ObjectRemoved:*
  thumbnails:
    handler: handler.thumbnails
    events:
      - s3:
          bucket: my-service-${sls:stage}-photos
          event: s3:ObjectCreated:*
          rules:
            - prefix: images/
```

S3 rejects two configurations on one bucket when their event types overlap (for example `s3:ObjectCreated:*` and `s3:ObjectCreated:Put`) and their `prefix` and `suffix` rules overlap as well; a configuration without `rules` overlaps every other one. In the example, `users` and `thumbnails` both use `s3:ObjectCreated:*` and stay valid because their prefixes, `uploads/` and `images/`, don't overlap.

## Configure the bucket with `provider.s3`

To set properties of a bucket the Framework creates, such as versioning or encryption, define it under `provider.s3` and use its key as the `s3` event's bucket:

```yaml
provider:
  name: aws
  s3:
    photos:
      name: my-service-${sls:stage}-photos
      versioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      bucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256

functions:
  resize:
    handler: handler.resize
    events:
      - s3: photos
```

- `name` sets the bucket name. Without `name`, the key (`photos`) is the bucket name, so it must follow the bucket naming rules. Set the name with `name` rather than `bucketName`: the Framework builds the Lambda permission from `name` or the key.
- The other keys are the properties of [AWS::S3::Bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-s3-bucket.html), with the first letter in lowercase (`bucketEncryption`, `versioningConfiguration`). Values below them keep CloudFormation's PascalCase (`Status`, `ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration`).
- The bucket's CloudFormation logical ID is `S3Bucket` followed by the key without non-alphanumeric characters and with its first letter in uppercase (`S3BucketPhotos`).

## Use an existing bucket

To add a notification to a bucket that already exists, outside this service's stack, set the `s3` event's `existing` to `true`:

```yaml
functions:
  users:
    handler: handler.users
    events:
      - s3:
          bucket: legacy-photos
          event: s3:ObjectCreated:*
          rules:
            - prefix: uploads/
            - suffix: .jpg
          existing: true
```

- The Framework adds a custom resource, backed by an extra Lambda function and IAM role in the stack, that writes the function's notification configurations to the bucket and adds the Lambda permission for S3. It keeps the bucket's other notification configurations, and removes the function's own configurations when the event or the service is removed.
- With `existing: true`, `bucket` can also be a CloudFormation intrinsic function, such as `!Ref` to a parameter or `!ImportValue`. Without `existing: true`, `bucket` must be a name.
- One function can use one existing bucket. `s3` events of one function on two different existing buckets stop packaging with `Only one S3 Bucket can be configured per function.`; use a separate function for each bucket.
- `event` and `rules` work as for a new bucket.

### Force an update of existing bucket notifications

The custom resource updates the bucket's notification configuration only when the `s3` event's settings change. If the configuration on the bucket was changed outside the Framework, set `forceDeploy: true` to rewrite it on every deploy:

```yaml
functions:
  users:
    handler: handler.users
    events:
      - s3:
          bucket: legacy-photos
          event: s3:ObjectCreated:*
          existing: true
          forceDeploy: true
```

`forceDeploy` takes effect only together with `existing: true`. The Framework reads `forceDeploy` from the function's first `s3` event with `existing: true`, and it rewrites all of that function's notification configurations on the bucket; set it on that event.

## `s3` event options

The `s3` event takes a bucket name, or an object with these keys:

| Key           | Type                    | Default              | Allowed values                                                                         |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bucket`      | String or intrinsic     | Required             | A bucket name or a `provider.s3` key; an intrinsic function only with `existing: true` |
| `event`       | String                  | `s3:ObjectCreated:*` | An S3 event type starting with `s3:`                                                   |
| `rules`       | List of one-key objects | Not set              | `prefix` or `suffix`, each a string or intrinsic function                              |
| `existing`    | Boolean                 | `false`              | `true` adds the notification to an existing bucket                                     |
| `forceDeploy` | Boolean                 | `false`              | `true` rewrites the notification configuration on every deploy; with `existing: true`  |

## Permissions for S3 events

For each function and bucket, the Framework adds an `AWS::Lambda::Permission` that lets `s3.amazonaws.com` invoke the function, limited to the bucket's ARN and the service's AWS account. The bucket and the function must be in the same AWS Region.

The function's execution role gets no access to the bucket. To read or write objects, add a statement to `provider.iam.role.statements`, and build the bucket ARN from its name: a `!GetAtt` or `!Ref` to a bucket the Framework creates makes the execution role depend on the bucket, which already depends on the function, and CloudFormation reports a circular dependency.

```yaml
provider:
  iam:
    role:
      statements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action: s3:GetObject
          Resource: arn:aws:s3:::my-service-${sls:stage}-photos/*
```

See [IAM permissions](../guide/iam.md).
